searchText: Hm.. I looked at it now. It seems to be highly susceptible to griefing? and yes, I realize it's not a "huge problem now", and it probably won't ever be, but seems a bit flaky to build on something which _could_ so easily be attacked, no? 120Mb of witnesses -- for what? I mean, how many blocks? (ah, you mean hte last 256 blocks a'la 0.5Mb each) yes, 256 blocks griefing as in building special calls that touch a lot of accounts? before eip2929 for sure cold storage load is 2100 account is 2600 so you can touch maybe 6000 storage items in a block they start to have common paths after a while so the growth should be sublinear if you start touching multiple accounts then the cost is higher but you can span out more on the accounts trie so probably the most efficient attackw ould be touching around 5000 accounts? 5000 accounts with ~6depth (unless attack is crafted to maximize depths) 30000 items? times 32bytes? 1MB? maybe 2MB and that is only on servers I think it is far from the worst and the witness does not require any complex construction I think it is fine for a version 0 protocol that can be experimented with and then improved to provide different witness formats what is cool is that we can already test witness creation and witness sharing mechanisms No, griefing as in serving a huge pile of useless hashes over the protocol Right, so this protocol is not meant to support stateless clients (yet), the idea being that the worst a griefer can do is slow down a new node from syncing Also, if a peer feeds you false hashes, you will know after a single block import. A false hash can be treated as malicious, and that peer can be ignored for future block imports. Then if we start considering it to be critical infrastructure, we could encode a commitment to the metawitness in the header If there are enough people using the protocol to make it worth someone griefing that is a good problem to have (IMHO) since it means there is real demand for stateless/beam Who is hurt by the griefing? The people trying to run stateless clients, or the people running stateless clients? Clients trying to beam sync Right, it would be too easy to halt any stateless client that you connect to by giving them a bunch of false hashes. To use something like this for stateless clients, we would definitely want some commitment embedded in the header Beam sync is a low-stakes way to experiment with how to specify witnesses & meta-witnesses as we work toward statelessness (eg~ list of hashes? List of accounts/a storage? List of partial paths? Something something SSZ? etc) this can be sorted out by including the hash in the header (as suggested above) not exactly this -> when you execute the block you actually can verify if someone suggested you wrong hashes and you can punish them
